newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 4.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Prosecutors to summon about 60 public servants for questioning about their alleged involvement in various irregularities including bribe-taking in return for favours for large-scale building projects.
- Prosecutors investigate real estate speculation by owners of some Seoul intra-city bus companies with embezzled money.
- Seoul city government considers lowering intra-city bus fare in wake of embezzlement scandals involving some bus company owners.
- Government watchdog agency launches special investigation of budget implementation by local autonomous councils.
- Projected Seoul-Pusan high-speed railway line is drawn on abandoned mining tunnels at 12 points where experts say cave-ins could be possible.
- The Japanese government has asked the South Korean government to stop the construction of a pier at the disputed Tok-do Islands, but the Korean side snubbed the Tokyo bid.
